'''Cloja''', officially the '''Republic of Cloja''', is a country in [[West Massir]]. It comprises the [[Clojan islans]], and the islands of [[Suro]] and [[Owiaq]], for a total land area of [[List of countries and dependencies by area|1,325 square kilometres (512 sq mi)]]. Cloja shares a maritime border with [[North Ayre]] to the west and [[Oyreain]] to the south. [[Kezapi]], on the west coast of the main island, is its capital and largest city.

Cloja was settled over time by various [[Oyreains poeples|Oyreains]] and [[Dahens peoples|Dahen peoples]], which created a diverse mix of cultures and languages linked to [[Massir]] and [[New Ayre]]. Cloja has been settled since the 10th century, it came under [[Taval|Tavalan]], and in the beginning of the 15th century, it became the [[Easuhura|Easuhuran]] colony of [[Navevor]] colony until 1714. Internal conflict preceded a unilateral declaration of independence and a [[North Ayre|North Ayrean]] invasion and annexation. The subsequent [[Ayrean occupation]] was characterised by extreme abuses of human rights, including torture and massacres, a series of events named the [[Clojan genocide]]. Resistance continued throughout Ayrean rule and in 1740, a [[Dahen–sponsored act of self-determinatio]]<nowiki/>n led North Ayre to relinquish control of the territory. Cloja became a new sovereign state in June of 1744. That same year, relations with [[North Ayre]] were established and normalised.

The national government is a [[Wikipedia:Unitary_parliamentary_republic|unitary parliamentary republic.]] Power is centralised under the national government, although many local leaders have informal influence. The country maintains a policy of international cooperation and is a member of the [[Massiran Association for Regional Cooperation|Massiran Association for Regional Cooperation (MARC)]], the [[Massiran Economic fund|Massiran Economic Fund,]] the [[Global Development Bank]], and the [[Global Trade Union]]. It is an informal member of [[SDSA]] and is an observer of the [[EISA]]. The country remains relatively rich, with an economy that relies heavily on tourism and shipping.

The total [[List of countries and dependencies by population|population is over 47,000]] at the 1764 census, and is heavily skewed towards old people due to a very low fertility rate. Education has led to increasing literacy over the past half-century, especially in the two official languages of [[Dahen language|Dahen]] and [[Lastnu language|Lastnu]]. High ethnic and linguistic diversity is reflected by the [[12 indigenous languages]] spoken in the country. Most of the population is _____, which coexists alongside strong local traditions and beliefs, especially in rural areas.
